input.goal: Our new muffler cut noise but backpressure went up 15%. We need the noise down without the backpressure.
failed: Tried a bigger pipe: too loud
input.idea: A straight-through perforated muffler with a Helmholtz resonator coupled through the perforations to kill the low-frequency boom without adding backpressure

US5365025A.quote: a tubular member having imperforate inlet and outlet end portions and a perforate central portion arranged along a central longitudinal axis
US5365025A.why: Straight-through perforated core keeps backpressure low while reactive + dissipative chambers take the noise: exactly the conflict.

US3754619A.quote: perforated tube means in said central apertures defining a gas flow path through the bodies
US3754619A.why: 1971 root of the straight-through idea: the gas never leaves a straight perforated path.

US7281605B2.quote: a Helmholtz resonator comprising a chamber and a throat positioned within said body, wherein said exhaust duct is a perforated exhaust duct and at least one perforation is acoustically coupled to said resonator throat
US7281605B2.why: Adds a low-frequency Helmholtz resonator to a straight-through dissipative silencer without blocking the flow.

US4111279A.quote: attenuating a preselected low frequency sound
US4111279A.why: Tuned resonator chamber for one low frequency; the flow passes outside the resonator.

US6792907B1.quote: controlling at least one of a volume of the chamber, a length of the neck portion, and a diameter of the neck portion responsive to the speed sensed by said engine speed sensor
US6792907B1.why: Tracks the firing frequency as rpm changes; adds actuators and cost.

US7798286B2.quote: the pressure waves having at least one objectionable wave having an objectionable amplitude and an objectionable frequency
US7798286B2.why: Targets the objectionable frequency but says little about backpressure.

US7243757B2.quote: a plurality of curved sound reflective baffles
US7243757B2.why: Baffles quiet the gas but add restriction: the opposite of the conflict.

US8439159B1.why: (canned model output with a quote that is NOT on the page: kept to show the quote check)

US4150732A.quote: said cavities thus forming annular acoustic resonators which attenuate, in a given frequency range, the acoustical energy propagating in the channel
US4150732A.why: Gas-turbine ducts: resonators sit flush in the wall, so the flow channel stays open (no added backpressure).

US3983955A.quote: the air in said chambers comprising spring means and the air in said openings comprising mass means
US3983955A.why: Classic mass-spring resonator panel; general acoustics, not hot gas.

US4222414A.quote: said elongate member being radially expandable at said wall portion when pulses occur in said flow line
US4222414A.why: Lab-instrument pulse damper: a compliant wall swallows each pulse with no restriction in the flow path.

US5996733A.quote: A side branch resonator for attenuating sound waves at first and second frequencies
US5996733A.why: Side branch off the main duct: cancels two frequencies with zero restriction in the flow.

US9394864B2.quote: defining a tube effective length that is less than the overall length
US9394864B2.why: Quarter-wave tube whose effective length can be switched: tunes the cancellation without touching the main flow.

US5849251A.quote: a tailpipe catalytic converter for installing in said exhaust tailpipe
US5849251A.why: Cited the 1992 root for relieving back pressure, but it is a catalyst, not noise control.

US7281605B2.quote: wherein said exhaust duct is a perforated exhaust duct and at least one perforation is acoustically coupled to said resonator throat
US7281605B2.why: Claims almost exactly the idea: a Helmholtz resonator coupled through the perforated straight-through duct. Strong prior art.

US5365025A.quote: a tubular member having imperforate inlet and outlet end portions and a perforate central portion arranged along a central longitudinal axis
US5365025A.why: Straight-through perforated core with reactive chambers; no Helmholtz neck claimed.

US4111279A.quote: substantially imperforate partition means forming a resonator chamber in the housing
US4111279A.why: Resonator chamber for a preselected low frequency, 1976.

US6792907B1.quote: a neck portion adapted to provide fluid communication between the chamber and a duct
US6792907B1.why: Helmholtz on a duct, tuned with rpm; not through the perforations.

US7243757B2.quote: a resonator inlet tube for said resonator chamber
US7243757B2.why: Resonator chamber, but the flow goes through baffles.

US3754619A.quote: perforated tube means in said central apertures defining a gas flow path through the bodies
US3754619A.why: Straight-through perforated path, 1971; no resonator neck.

US5849251A.quote: a tailpipe catalytic converter for installing in said exhaust tailpipe

US7798286B2.quote: the pressure waves having at least one objectionable wave having an objectionable amplitude and an objectionable frequency
US7798286B2.why: Targets one objectionable frequency, but no resonator coupled through perforations.

US5996733A.quote: A side branch resonator for attenuating sound waves at first and second frequencies
US5996733A.why: Two frequencies from one branch: hit 100 Hz and 200 Hz with a short tube.

US9394864B2.quote: defining a tube effective length that is less than the overall length
US9394864B2.why: Switchable effective length: a short tube tuned to the 2nd harmonic fits the 1.0 m limit.

US6814041B1.quote: a first of said channels having a first length between an entrance and a terminating end
US6814041B1.why: Several molded channels of different lengths: folds the length into a flat part.

US5365025A.quote: a tubular member having imperforate inlet and outlet end portions and a perforate central portion arranged along a central longitudinal axis
US5365025A.why: Still the backpressure baseline, but it does not solve the 1.0 m packaging limit.

US6792907B1.quote: controlling at least one of a volume of the chamber, a length of the neck portion, and a diameter of the neck portion responsive to the speed sensed by said engine speed sensor
US6792907B1.why: Tunable, but a Helmholtz cavity this low is bulky.

US4222414A.quote: said elongate member being radially expandable at said wall portion when pulses occur in said flow line
US4222414A.why: Compliant wall idea; hot gas limits materials.

US3754619A.quote: perforated tube means in said central apertures defining a gas flow path through the bodies
US3754619A.why: Backpressure root; says nothing about short side branches.

wildcard.principle: smooth 100 Hz pressure pulses in a hot flowing gas (~400 °C, c ≈ 510 m/s)

ideas.mechanism: quarter-wave tube coiled like a French horn
ideas.transfer: A closed side tube a quarter-wavelength long cancels the 100 Hz pulse. Coil it like a French horn so 1.28 m fits under the car.

evidence.title: US2484408A French horn (1945): “the usual coil intermediate said ends”

ideas.mechanism: slide-whistle piston that changes the tube length
ideas.transfer: A slide whistle retunes by moving a piston. Do the same in the side branch so the cancellation follows rpm.

evidence.title: US2617324A Combined confection and whistle (1950): a lollipop slide whistle

ideas.mechanism: Windkessel: a compliant chamber that stores each pulse and releases it smoothly
ideas.transfer: The aorta stretches on each heartbeat and smooths the pulse. Put a compliant chamber on the exhaust so pulses are absorbed instead of choked.

evidence.title: Westerhof et al. (2009), The arterial Windkessel, Med Biol Eng Comput

ideas.transfer: A Helmholtz bottle tuned to 100 Hz on a short neck.

evidence.title: US3983955A Arrangement for damping sound with resonators (1973)

ideas.mechanism: serrated feather edges that quiet airflow
ideas.transfer: Owls fly silently thanks to serrated feather edges. Serrate the tailpipe outlet?

evidence.title: Owl-inspired leading-edge serrations for aerodynamic noise reduction (Physics of Fluids, 2025)
Bio-inspired trailing-edge serrations: noise down in the 1600–5000 Hz band (Applied Acoustics, 2022)

test_results: Prototype 2: straight-through perforated core + a 1.3 m coiled quarter-wave side branch: backpressure back to baseline, 100 Hz boom down 9 dB
Packaging review: only 1.0 m of side-branch tube fits next to the fuel tank
